name: manage_transcript
description:
Manage source transcript fixes and deprecated low-level transcript variant inspection. Finding timestamps remains in `find_transcript`. Captions own viewer-facing translation behavior.

For ordinary user-facing requests like "turn on bilingual captions", "translate my captions to English", or "show Chinese + English subtitles", use `edit_captions` action `translate`. It explicitly creates/refreshes the translation and switches caption visibility in one caption-tool call. In those requests, `languageCode` / `targetLanguage` means the TRANSLATION TARGET language, not the original language: English original + Chinese/English captions means target `zh`, not `en`.

# Actions

## fix
Correct ASR mistakes or speaker assignments in an asset's **source** transcript. This changes transcript truth only; it does not edit timeline playback or remove audible content.

Input fields: `asset` required; `content` required with FIX / SPEAKER commands; optional `preview`.

`content` command format, one command per line:
- `FIX [sN]: wordIdx -> "newText"` — replace EXACTLY ONE word: the word at 0-based `wordIdx` within segment `[sN]` (segment ids exactly as shown in read_script's timeline.md / library files) becomes `newText`; every other word in the segment is untouched. To change several words, write one FIX per word — never put a whole phrase into a single FIX. Examples: segment `[s3] I'm Ben Atkins here` → `FIX [s3]: 2 -> "Adkins"`; segment `[s8] 从肚子到杯子到底经历了什么` → `FIX [s8]: 1 -> "豆子"` (only 肚子 changes; CJK words are indexed by the same whitespace/word tokens shown in read_script).
- `SPEAKER [sN]: name` or `SPEAKER [sN-sM]: name` — assign those segments to a speaker (created if missing). Example: `SPEAKER [s2-s6]: Alice`.
Timestamps and text-search forms (`FIX "old" -> "new"`) are NOT accepted. Before any multi-command batch, and whenever unsure of wordIdx, run with `preview: true` first — it shows the old word each command would touch without writing, so a wrong index can never become a bad write.

To rename an existing diarized speaker label everywhere (e.g. "that's Jon, not John"), do not reassign segments — use `edit_project` action `speaker-update` with the speaker id returned by the transcript workflow.

## retry_transcription
Force-retry ASR for an audio/video asset after transcription is stuck, timed out, or failed. Input fields: `asset` required. External MCP agents that already hold prepared audio bytes may pass `audioBase64` plus `audioMimeType` and optional `audioFilename` / `audioStartTimestampSec`; ChatCut uploads that audio and uses it for the retry. This bypasses backend duplicate locks safely and starts a new fenced transcription run; it does not wait for completion. Before reading transcript/captions, call `track_progress` once with `target: "transcription"`, `action: "status"`, and the returned asset id. If it is non-terminal, check again only after the returned interval.

## translation_list / translation_read
Inspect original + translation transcript variants for a source scope. Pass `json` with exactly one scope: `assetId`, `itemId`, `trackId`, or `allSpoken:true`. `translation_read` can include `targetLanguage` to narrow one language.

## Scope window semantics
`itemId`, `trackId`, and `allSpoken` only translate the speech the timeline actually USES — the source-media window each item plays (its in/out trim), not the whole asset. So a 1-hour source with only a 1-minute clip on the timeline translates roughly that minute's sentences, picked at full sentence boundaries (never a half sentence). `assetId` is the explicit "translate the ENTIRE asset" escape hatch — use it when you deliberately want the whole source covered regardless of what's on the timeline.

## translation_ensure
Deprecated write-only transcript-variant preparation: translates only the in-window sentences that are missing OR stale (source edited since translation), and reuses the ones already translated and current — no LLM cost for those. This is for compatibility/debugging only. Materialized captions do not read these rows for viewer-facing translation; use `edit_captions translate`, which writes `captions_item.translations` on caption cards. The result reports `translatedUtteranceCount` (new/changed sentences translated this run) and `skippedExistingUtteranceCount` (already-current sentences reused).

## translation_create
Force-regenerate the in-window transcript-variant sentences for `targetLanguage`, overwriting their prior translation rows. Existing translations for sentences OUTSIDE this scope's window are left intact. Compatibility/debugging only; ordinary caption retranslation must use `edit_captions translate` with `force:true` so card-owned translations update.

# Translation scope json examples
- `{"trackId":"V1","targetLanguage":"en"}` — only the speech V1's items keep
- `{"source":{"assetId":"<id>"},"targetLanguage":"es","sourceLanguage":"en"}` — the whole asset
- `{"allSpoken":true,"targetLanguage":"en"}` — every used window across the timeline

# Translation result
`translation_ensure` and `translation_create` are lower-level compatibility actions. They return `captionVisibility.visibleInCaptions:false` and no longer return a caption-visibility follow-up. For normal agent behavior, do not chain these manually; call `edit_captions translate`. Do not invent a captions source shape and do not store translations in caption word overrides.

# Translation reliability
The model translates sentence-delimited transcript chunks naturally; the backend computes caption word rows locally for rendering. Silence markers are preserved locally. If a batch misses any sentence, the backend retries missing sentences one-by-one before writing rows. If any speech sentence is still missing after retry, the action fails as a full or partial translation failure; treat either as no usable translation write and retry once or narrow the scope.

action.description: One of: fix, retry_transcription, translation_create, translation_ensure, translation_list, translation_read

asset.description: For action=fix or retry_transcription: asset id/prefix.

audioBase64.description: For action=retry_transcription: optional prepared audio bytes as base64 or a data:audio/...;base64 URL. External MCP only; use when the asset has no remoteUrl or you already extracted audio.

audioFilename.description: For action=retry_transcription with audioBase64: optional filename, e.g. extracted-audio.wav.

audioMimeType.description: For action=retry_transcription with audioBase64: MIME type, e.g. audio/wav, audio/mpeg, audio/ogg, audio/mp4, audio/webm.

audioStartTimestampSec.description: For action=retry_transcription with audioBase64: optional source-video timestamp offset for the first audio sample.

content.description: For action=fix: FIX / SPEAKER commands, newline-separated, e.g. FIX [s3]: 2 -> "word" | SPEAKER [s2-s5]: Alice. Segment ids are the [sN] ids from read_script; wordIdx is the 0-based index of the ONE word to replace (newText replaces that word only, not a span). Run preview:true before a batch.

json.description: JSON with exactly one scope plus targetLanguage for write actions. Example: {"trackId":"V1","targetLanguage":"en"}.

preview.description: For action=fix: preview only, no changes applied.

projectId.description: Existing project ID from the editor URL or list_projects. Pass this when continuing work on an existing project and the external MCP session is not already targeted.
